title: BECE Basic Science - Basic Science - Energy
subject: Basic Science

options: The force applied to an object
questions.explain: In physics, energy is formally defined as the capacity or ability to perform work.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position is called:
questions.explain: Potential energy (specifically gravitational potential energy) depends on the height (position) of an object.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following energy changes occurs in an electric iron?
questions.explain: An electric iron consumes electricity and converts it into heat to iron clothes.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The S.I. unit of energy is the:
questions.explain: The Joule (J) is the standard International System of Units (SI) unit for energy and work.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
questions.explain: Petroleum is a fossil fuel which is finite and cannot be replenished on a human timescale.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The formula for calculating Kinetic Energy (K.E.) is:
questions.explain: Kinetic Energy is calculated as one-half the mass times the square of the velocity ($$ \frac{1}{2} mv^2 $$).
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Conduction is the method of heat transfer primarily in:
questions.explain: Conduction requires direct contact of particles, which is most effective in solids where particles are closely packed.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: What type of energy is stored in a dry cell battery?
questions.explain: Batteries store energy in chemical bonds, which is converted to electrical energy when used.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The primary source of energy for the Earth is the:
questions.explain: The Sun provides solar energy, which drives Earth's climate and supports almost all life.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The law of conservation of energy states that:
options: Energy can be created but not destroyed
Energy can be destroyed but not created
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
questions.explain: The law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
questions.subject: Basic Science
